title: Bar Ada Savula’ah

paragraphs: Mentioned in [Bava Metzia 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.93b.11): he was taking animals over the bridge at Naresh. One pushed another into the water. He came before Rav Papa, who ordered him to pay compensation.[^1]
Apparently he was merely a herdsman and was not counted among the Torah scholars.[^2]

notes.text: [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Metzia.93b.11.1) glosses the expression as “the bridge of Naresh.” The linked passage continues with Rav Papa’s answer that the animals should have been led across one at a time.
[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=243&lang=en) recounts the same case and says he does not know whether Bar Ada was a sage. Hyman calls his own characterization probable.
